summary: Iteration 4 verified: (1) two-user login ('158' and 'IT admin'), (2) manual purchase_date on create/update, (3) PUT/DELETE now require auth (401 otherwise), (4) approval still gated. Backend: 63/63 pytest tests pass (11 new cases in test_manual_date_and_auth.py + updated regression tests in backend_test.py and test_auth_bill.py to send Bearer token for PUT/DELETE). Frontend E2E via Playwright covered all requested flows: logged-out Add form shows required manual date picker defaulting to today, chosen date persists on the created row (Jan 15, 2026), row shows 'Login to edit' (readonly-{id}) and no edit/delete buttons; login as 'IT admin' reveals header username, select-all checkbox, per-row edit/delete; edit changes purchase_date (2026-03-20) and persists; approval toggle works; delete via confirm dialog works; logout hides edit/delete and restores readonly labels; login as '158' also works.
action_items: Optional cleanup: preview DB has accumulated many TEST_* records from prior iterations (~50). Consider a cleanup script or DELETE endpoint for TEST_ prefix (would need auth).
critical_code_review_comments: Auth model is simple hardcoded users via env; JWT is HS256 with a fixed secret. Fine for internal RLPC use case but note: brute-force is not rate-limited and JWT_SECRET must be rotated if leaked.
AUTH_USERS built once at module import — adding a third user in .env requires a backend restart (documented supervisor behavior).

create_purchase accepts purchase_date as free-form string (no validation). If a client sends a malformed value (e.g. 'yesterday'), it will be stored verbatim and later sorts/date filters could misbehave. Consider validating with datetime.fromisoformat() in the endpoint.
update_purchase: when purchase_date is not provided in body it correctly preserves existing value (pop returns None, guarded by 'if purchase_date'). Verified by regression test.
PurchaseUpdate inherits all required fields from PurchaseBase — clients must resend the full record on edit. That's how the UI works today, but a PATCH-style partial update would be more idiomatic.
delete_purchase requires auth but does not check that the record exists before the DELETE — MongoDB update returns deleted_count=0 which maps to 404; correct behavior.
server.py still uses deprecated @app.on_event startup/shutdown handlers (carry-over).
test_credentials: Users: '158' / 'Rlpc_974' and 'IT admin' / 'Rlpc_974' (space in username). Login endpoint: POST /api/auth/login, returns {token, username}. Bearer token in Authorization header.
seed_data_creation: Each test creates TEST_* prefixed records and deletes them via authenticated session in teardown. UI E2E created one TEST_UI4_<ts>_ record and cleaned it up via the app's own delete flow.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests split across 4 files under /app/backend/tests/: backend_test.py (CRUD/filters/exports — PUT/DELETE now use auth_session), test_auth_bill.py (bill upload/download, Safety Shoes, approval gating: PUT without token now returns 401 not 403), test_bulk_approval.py (bulk endpoint), test_manual_date_and_auth.py (new: two-user login, manual date, PUT/DELETE 401 without token). Run: pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v. Note the username 'IT admin' contains a space. Manual date input (data-testid=input-purchase-date) is type=date and stored as `${date}T00:00:00`; table renders via toLocaleString so 2026-01-15T00:00:00 appears as 'Jan 15, 2026, 12:00 AM'.
